page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The email
title: The email
description:
Anna's having trouble with her emails. She's been trying to sort out the order of Imperial Lemons for Mr Lime. She sends an email but her choice of text-speak isn't appropriate and Paul, the boss, isn't impressed.
Anna needs some help from Tom who always has plenty of advice. Her email is rewritten and sent off, but will that be the end of the matter?
This episode focuses on the correct language to use in an email.

listening_challenge.question: What is Anna trying to confirm in her email?
listening_challenge.answer: That her company can provide 300 luxury boxes to Mr Lime.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello, Anna's just arrived at her desk to start the day at Tip Top Trading. Paul is walking towards her, eating a biscuit, he looks a bit bothered.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, Paul.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text:
Come and have a biscuit in my office.
Now Anna, about Mr Lime.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I didn't say yes!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Pardon? Yes to what?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, nothing.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: You sent him an email yesterday and copied me in.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Your email reads: boxes ok. pls c-d-u cfirm wnt 300 ta.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes: please could you confirm you want 300.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Right. Now that's not really the best way of writing an email to a client, is it?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Please could you re-send your message to Mr Lime, using actual words that make sense.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Thank you. Have a chocolate crunchy!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Morning Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hello.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Let me guess, Paul just spoke to you about your email?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: How do you know?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You copied me in remember, I just read it – or tried to.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But what's the problem? Other people write like that!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No, maybe some people write text messages like that in an SMS message on their phones, but that is completely the wrong style for an email to a client.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Okay Anna, let's stop listening to Tom, he's a waste of space. These are the kinds of phrases you need in a business-related email:
Dear Mr Lime...
I hope you are well.
I am writing regarding...
Please could you confirm...
Yours sincerely, or
Best wishes.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you! I'll rewrite my message. There! I'd better get it checked before I send. Denise?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: (On the phone) yes... the other problem with Stephanie is that her legs are just too long...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, she's on the phone.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: ... yes, like trees...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'll have to ask Tom. Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Mm?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Could you read this through before I send it?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hang on, Anna, let me just finish this sentence. It’s really important. I’m ready, let’s have a look. Okay. (reading) Dear Mr Lime, I hope you are well. I am writing regarding your request for luxury boxes for the Imperial Lemon Delivery. We will indeed be able to supply them. Please could you confirm that you want 300. Best wishes, Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It’s good, it's much better. Send it. Hopefully Mr Lime will think your last message was just someone sitting on your keyboard by mistake.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You're not...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Nothing. It's none of my business.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You're not ever going to go to lunch with Mr Lime are you? I mean, in a non-business way...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No of course not!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I mean I don’t care… it's just... important to... stay professional.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hmmm.... well, I had a feeling Anna's email was going to cause problems. But at least she won't make a mistake like that again. Here’s a reminder of the phrases she used in her new, improved email.
Until next time, bye!
